data: {"content_index":0,"item_id":"","logprobs":[],"output_index":1,"sequence_number":407,"text":"## Purpose\n\nA production HTTP gateway should enforce separate connection, first-byte, idle-stream, and total-request timeouts because each protects a different phase of the request lifecycle. The connection timeout limits how long the gateway waits to establish a TCP/TLS connection to an upstream. The first-byte timeout bounds the time until the upstream begins responding. The idle-stream timeout protects long-lived or streaming responses by requiring continued progress. The total-request timeout caps the entire operation so resources are not held indefinitely. These limits are complementary; one timeout cannot safely replace the others without either killing valid traffic too early or allowing stalled work to consume capacity.\n\n## Failure modes\n\nDifferent failures appear at different phases. A connection timeout handles unreachable hosts, SYN backlog exhaustion, DNS misrouting, or TLS handshakes that never complete. A first-byte timeout catches accepted requests where the upstream is overloaded, deadlocked, or waiting on a slow dependency before producing headers. An idle-stream timeout detects partial streaming responses that start successfully but then stop sending data, which a first-byte timeout would no longer cover. A total-request timeout prevents slow-but-active transfers from running forever, even if they periodically send bytes and never trip the idle timeout.\n\n## Operational guidance\n\nWhen a timeout fires, the gateway should propagate cancellation downstream so upstream services stop work, database queries can be aborted, and request-scoped resources are released. It should also clean up connection-pool state correctly: close poisoned, half-closed, or timed-out sockets rather than returning them to the pool, while preserving healthy reusable connections when protocol semantics allow. Timeout values should be chosen from service-level objectives, upstream latency profiles, payload size, and streaming behavior, with metrics that identify which phase expired. Avoid masking one timeout with another; for example, a generous total timeout does not protect the connect path, and an idle timeout does not bound total duration.\n\nOperational rule: define, measure, and enforce a distinct timeout for every request phase, and treat timeout expiry as cancellation plus connection-state cleanup.","type":"response.output_text.done"}

A total-request timeout prevents slow-but-active transfers from running forever, even if they periodically send bytes and never trip the idle timeout.\n\n## Operational guidance\n\nWhen a timeout fires, the gateway should propagate cancellation downstream so upstream services stop work, database queries can be aborted, and request-scoped resources are released. It should also clean up connection-pool state correctly: close poisoned, half-closed, or timed-out sockets rather than returning them to the pool, while preserving healthy reusable connections when protocol semantics allow. Timeout values should be chosen from service-level objectives, upstream latency profiles, payload size, and streaming behavior, with metrics that identify which phase expired. Avoid masking one timeout with another; for example, a generous total timeout does not protect the connect path, and an idle timeout does not bound total duration.\n\nOperational rule: define, measure, and enforce a distinct timeout for every request phase, and treat timeout expiry as cancellation plus connection-state cleanup.","type":"output_text"}],"id":"","phase":"final_answer","role":"assistant","status":"completed","type":"message"}],"parallel_tool_calls":true,"presence_penalty":0,"previous_response_id":null,"prompt_cache_retention":"24h","reasoning":{"context":"current_turn","effort":"low","mode":"standard","summary":null},"safety_identifier":"3e80cba422577a1d05cbd9b2fda1f8a0f9508b1d59523f38058558e44fba47f8","service_tier":"default","status":"completed","store":false,"temperature":1,"text":{"format":{"type":"text"},"verbosity":"medium"},"tool_choice":"auto","tool_usage":{"image_gen":{"input_tokens":0,"input_tokens_details":{"image_tokens":0,"text_tokens":0},"output_tokens":0,"output_tokens_details":{"image_tokens":0,"text_tokens":0},"total_tokens":0},"web_search":{"num_requests":0}},"tools":[],"top_logprobs":0,"top_p":0.98,"truncation":"disabled","usage":{"input_tokens":83,"input_tokens_details":{"cache_write_tokens":0,"cached_tokens":0},"output_tokens":430,"output_tokens_details":{"reasoning_tokens":23},"total_tokens":513},"user":null},"sequence_number":410,"type":"response.completed"}
